attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10. Created a dedicated CA on node1, issued per-node server certs (CN=node1/node2/node3) and a client cert (CN=replicator) signed by that CA, and configured all three nodes' postgresql.conf (ssl=on with the CA-issued certs) plus pg_hba.conf to accept replication connections only via `hostssl ... cert` rules requiring a CA-signed client certificate — verified a cert-less connection is rejected with "connection requires a valid client certificate". Standbys were built with pg_basebackup -R over TLS using the replicator client cert (verify-full), and are streaming with ssl=t confirmed via pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl. Firewalld was opened for 5432/tcp on all nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for node1, node2, node3: captured pre-restart boot_id and health, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified PostgreSQL/replication/TLS/data recovered on each before moving to the next node. Final check after all restarts shows both standbys streaming over SSL and a post-restart test row replicated to both.
